title.en: Chase and sense games: Nakal Kho, Mai Bhi Maindhak, Bhukha Sher, Ghar Pehchano
The hungry lion and the frog

text.en: Some games make you copy, hop, roar or find soil with closed eyes! These four games sharpen your reflexes, observation and sense of direction.

Nakal Kho: form a large circle with defenders inside and one attacker. The attacker picks a defender to chase. The defender runs and does any action (jump, spin, crawl, clap, hop) and the attacker must copy it. A tired defender can stand before another defender and say Kho; the new defender runs and the attacker switches. If the attacker tags a defender, that student becomes the new attacker. There is no single winner.
Mai Bhi Maindhak: one student is the attacker (frog), squatting and hopping while trying to tag defenders with one hand. A tagged defender also becomes a frog. The last defender not tagged wins. Only gentle leg touches, no kicking.
Bhukha Sher: draw 2-foot circles with 7-8 students in each, 3 to 4 feet apart; these are safe areas. One student outside is the hungry lion (denner) who roars on all fours. When the denner names a wild animal, everyone comes out to chase and tap the lion's back; the one who taps becomes Veer. Suddenly the denner roars Bhakshanam (I want to eat) and all run back to their safe circles. Anyone caught becomes the next denner.
Ghar Pehchano: a student stands with palms joined holding soil. Another covers their eyes and leads them diagonally, left, right, forward and back, and the soil is dropped suddenly. They are led back with eyes closed to the start and have 5 to 15 seconds to find the soil while others try to hide it. If they fail, they do five sit-ups. It builds spatial sense and love for our soil.
Variations: begin with two or three frogs, change the word Bhakshanam to a word in your local language, or replace sit-ups with squats. Discuss strategies, safety and how it felt to be tagged.

problem.en: In Bhukha Sher what do students do when the denner roars Bhakshanam?

text.en: Everyone is outside chasing the lion.

why.en: The denner suddenly changes the game.

text.en: All students run back to their safe circles; anyone the lion catches becomes the next denner.

prompt.en: Explain the rules of Nakal Kho.

requiredIdeas.en: Defenders inside a circle, one attacker
Attacker copies the defender's action while chasing
A tired defender says Kho to switch; tagged student becomes attacker

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking there is a single winner

points.en: Nakal Kho: imitate actions; switch by saying Kho.
Mai Bhi Maindhak: tagged players become frogs; last defender wins.
Bhukha Sher: run to safe circles on Bhakshanam.
Ghar Pehchano: find the soil within 5 to 15 seconds or do five sit-ups.
